paragraphs:
This is not a summit trek or a race against the clock. It is a carefully paced journey for travellers who want to walk through Yunnan’s quieter mountain country while remaining connected to the people and places that shape it.
The main hike in Luoguqing can be adapted to the group, from a gentler woodland walk to a fuller day among grasslands, streams and rhododendron slopes. Before and after the trail, Lijiang and Shaxi bring the journey back to the old Tea Horse Road — through stone lanes, caravan history and evenings that invite you to slow down.

items.title: Walk through Yunnan’s wild rhododendron season
items.description: Follow a mountain road where rhododendrons bloom across entire hillsides, their colours changing with altitude, weather and light.

items.title: Choose a trail that feels right for you
items.description: Luoguqing offers more than one way into the landscape. Your local guide will shape the walking day around your experience, energy and current trail conditions.

items.title: Enter the landscapes of the Pumi people
items.description: The forests and grasslands around Luoguqing are also lived-in landscapes, shaped by generations of Pumi families, grazing animals and seasonal mountain life.

items.title: Let the journey slow down in Shaxi
items.description: After the mountains, spend a night in Shaxi, where the old theatre, stone lanes and Yujin Bridge still carry the quieter rhythm of the Tea Horse Road.

items.title: Travel privately and leave room for the unexpected
items.description: There are no shopping stops and no fixed group timetable. The journey can respond to the flowers, the weather and the way you prefer to walk.
